facts.raw_span: diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities
Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
Punch biopsy findings: Small organisms within vasculature
Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels
diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities
Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
Punch biopsy findings: Small organisms within vasculature
Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels

concepts.why: The patient has fever, elevated C-reactive protein, and evidence of small organisms within vasculature on biopsy, with Gram-positive cocci in vessels, consistent with Staphylococcal sepsis.
The patient has cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia on CT chest/abdomen.
The patient has areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys suspected to represent renal abscesses on CT chest/abdomen.
The patient has multifocal lesions, likely septic emboli on MRI brain.
The patient has purpuric retiform patches on each flank, consistent with Purpura fulminans.
The patient has elevated AST and ALT, and C-reactive protein, consistent with acute liver injury.

rationales.F06: Purpuric retiform patches are characteristic of Purpura fulminans and suggest Staphylococcal sepsis.
rationales.F10: Cavitary lesions in lungs are indicative of Necrotizing pneumonia.
rationales.F11: Small organisms within vasculature on biopsy suggest Staphylococcal sepsis and Purpura fulminans.
rationales.F12: Gram-positive cocci in vessels on tissue Gram staining are indicative of Staphylococcal sepsis and Purpura fulminans.

frontier_selector.rationale: Purpura fulminans best explains the purpuric retiform patches, bruises, and diffuse papules, with laboratory and imaging findings consistent with severe infection and organ dysfunction, while Staphylococcal sepsis is a close runner-up given the presence of gram-positive cocci and positive culture results.
